definitionOfDone: One scene graph produces docked-service, expedition-habitat and compact-flight silhouettes without swapping meshes.
The protected garden, Great Tree, occupied deck cassettes and garage reserve never intersect a moving shell or hinge envelope.
The compact pose is unmistakably controller-derived, remains medium/large-office-building scale and does not read as a city or handheld toy.
Named thrust, boost, hover-downwash, landing-light and camera sockets survive every pose.
Front, side, rear, top, three-quarter and phone-scale three-pose captures show no detached joints, inverted surfaces or hidden-volume collisions.

True human-eye-height cameras can stand on the garden floor and upper balcony without intersecting geometry, and both positions reveal a continuous multi-storey inhabited atrium with real fore-aft depth.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Side-by-side review shows correct concept and real volume, but a large gap in architectural density, leg construction, silhouette integration, and finish. This is honestly about 4/10, so refine-code is mandatory.

featureReviews.notes: Missing long grip masses and pinched controller waist.
Tree is present but the protected atrium and occupied ring are underscaled.
Four contacts exist but do not originate from the approved handle/rear-stabilizer architecture.
Current two-wing and belly-array propulsion contradicts the approved three-drive layout.
Current bubble shield lacks attached armor leaves, seam panels, and conformal emitters.

visualEvidence.notes: Formal refine-spec checkpoint after user selected the controller-derived shape, tri-drive mobility, and layered retractable shield references.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The existing render is a recognizable stylized walking habitat, but it is not yet the same designed object as the approved controller-shaped ship. This is a root specification mismatch, not a polishing problem.

featureReviews.notes: Broad bridge exists, but grips remain short loop forms and the waist is not clean enough.
Great Tree and protected central volume remain stable; identity is readable in Haven.
Powered front grip-legs and lighter rear stabilizers exist, but grip-to-leg continuity is incomplete.
Runtime contains the center keel and two gimballed grip drives, though the visual nozzle hierarchy needs clearer views.
Pressure window, four armor leaves, and conformal emitters are separate systems; Fast Space closure still leaks the sanctuary silhouette.
Tree and window bands imply habitation, but the blockout lacks enough deck depth and scale cues.

visualEvidence.notes: Use the comparison sheet as the authority. Numerical Tier 1 passed at IoU 0.8689, but its non-isolated-background warning prevents treating that score as visual acceptance.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Direct comparison shows the same concept and the correct system inventory, but not yet the same dominant shape. The reference is organized by two long controller grips and a low bridge; the render is organized by a tall central pod and two circular side masses. The automated IoU pass is non-authoritative here because its warning says most background pixels were included.

featureReviews.notes: Tapered white crowns now carry the roof identity.
Warm tree volume is clear but surrounding architecture is flat.
Four legs are present but lack concept-level articulation.
Side terraces deploy clearly with rails and planters.
Towers remain blocky and under-integrated.

visualEvidence.notes: Landscape framing and elevated camera now match the reference class; remaining mismatch is geometry and finish, not framing.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The macro controller/Walker concept is now recognizable, but the concept has much taller, denser articulated legs, genuinely inhabited multi-level side volumes, integrated tower architecture, and layered PBR surface detail. Current render remains a stylized blockout, roughly 4/10, so Tier 1 failure is directionally correct.

visualEvidence.notes: Tier-1 hard gate failed; no Tier-2 VLM rescue was run. Manual evidence inspection is used only to route the next code correction.

visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The primitive family is materially closer: a deep rectangular habitat is enclosed by white controller shoulders. The result is still one procedural-detail tier below the reference, with upright legs and balcony bars obscuring the garden.

visualEvidence.notes: Tier-1 hard gate still fails; route one final bounded correction to sanctuary openness.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The leg chain now has a deliberate hip-to-foot load path rather than hanging vertically. The change is visually correct but small relative to the remaining interior and mechanical-density gap.

visualEvidence.notes: The bounded 9-of-9 recovery ceiling is reached with the hard Tier-1 gate still failing; no completion claim or detail pass is authorized.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Moving the galleries to the perimeter creates the intended civic garden sightline and is a clear semantic improvement. The remaining gap is no longer center-room layout; it is primarily leg construction, roof hierarchy, mechanical layering, and surface response.

visualEvidence.notes: Tier-1 remains a hard failure; route only the roof and tower hierarchy next.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The leg system is more legible and engineering-like, especially at the exposed upper frame and layered shin. The larger remaining semantic failure is the flat roof and underscaled tower silhouette.

visualEvidence.notes: Tier-1 remains a hard failure; route the final bounded correction only to shoulder/hull connectivity.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The top now has meaningful vertical and inhabited structure. The next improvement should connect that roof hierarchy into the shoulders and side habitats through secondary structural ribs rather than add more isolated detail.

visualEvidence.notes: Manual review of the single packaged reference/render sheet. Tier-1 hard-fails and this refine-code result must not unlock the next sculpt pass.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The model now reads as one coherent transforming controller ship rather than a central room with detached shells. The shoulder gallery bands materially bridge the white arches to the habitat. The remaining gap is macro and systemic: the reference carries thicker leg masses, deeper nested load paths, varied occupied decks, fine surface segmentation, and cinematic material depth.

visualEvidence.notes: Manual review of the single packaged reference/render sheet; hard visual gates remain failed.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The increased leg volumes make the walker more credible and prevent the rear chain from disappearing, but the reference still has more articulated load paths and much richer occupied side volumes. The identical horizontal gallery modules are now the largest toy-like cue.

visualEvidence.notes: Manual review of the packaged reference/render sheet; visual acceptance remains failed.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The gallery rhythm is less repetitive and more architectural. The broad white shoulder faces and clean roof slab now read as the largest remaining toy-like surfaces; the next correction should use stepped overlap and seam depth rather than add small decoration.

visualEvidence.notes: Manual review of the packaged reference/render sheet. The IoU decrease is not chased because the roof improvement is visually valid and the cinematic reconstruction caveat applies.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The top now behaves as a connected spacecraft system and the towers no longer read as orange sticks. The model remains a clean stylized blockout beside a cinematic ultra-detailed reference. Reaching 10/10 will require a systemic panel truss bevel and material language, not another isolated proportional tweak.
